content: Rockland Paramedic Services (RPS) is a non-profit organization established through the collaboration of Good Samaritan and Nyack Hospitals. Its purpose is to deliver state-of-the-art Advanced Life Support (ALS) Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to the residents of Haverstraw, Stony Point, Clarkstown, Ramapo, and Orangetown in Rockland County, New York. In 1996, their services expanded to include the Town of Tuxedo in Orange County. RPS was officially formed in 1991 following the merger of the paramedic programs of Nyack Hospital and Good Samaritan Hospital. Prior to this, both hospitals operated separate paramedic fly-car services, with Nyack Hospital covering the eastern half of Rockland County and Good Samaritan Hospital covering the western half. Patient transport was handled by local volunteer ambulance corps. The population served by RPS is 304,064, and their response area spans 246 square miles. RPS has achieved several notable firsts in the region: It was the first organization in Orange and Rockland Counties to be certified as an Advanced Life Support First Responder. It developed the first comprehensive 12-lead EKG program in New York State. It was the first to implement cellular telemetry in New York State. It introduced the first Bike Medic Program in New York State. It was the first to obtain EMT-D certification for volunteer corps in Rockland County. It conducted the first EMT-Intermediate programs in Rockland County. It established the first Fire Department Rehabilitation Program in Rockland County. RPS operates seven Medic units stationed in various communities: Medic 1 responds to 911 calls in Haverstraw and Stony Point, including Bear Mountain State Park, working with the Haverstraw Volunteer Ambulance Corps and Stony Point Volunteer Ambulance Corps. Medic 3 serves the Town of Clarkstown, collaborating with New City Volunteer Ambulance Corps, Congers-Valley Cottage Volunteer Ambulance Corps, and Nanuet Ambulance Corps. Medic 5 covers Clarkstown and Orangetown, working with Nanuet Volunteer Ambulance Corps, Nyack Volunteer Ambulance Corps, and Congers-Valley Cottage Volunteer Ambulance Corps. Medic 21 responds to calls in Orangetown, partnering with Pearl River Alumni VAC, South Orangetown Volunteer Ambulance Corps, and Piermont Fire Department. Medic 23 serves the Town of Ramapo, working with Ramapo Valley Volunteer Ambulance Corps, William P. Faist Volunteer Ambulance Corps, Sloatsburg Volunteer Ambulance Corps, and Hatzolah Volunteer Ambulance Corps. Medic 25 also serves Ramapo, collaborating with Spring Hill Volunteer Ambulance Corps and Hatzolah Volunteer Ambulance Corps. Medic 31 responds to calls in the Town of Tuxedo, working with Tuxedo Volunteer Ambulance Corps. The RPS Special Operations Division was launched in September 2002 to address the need for specialized medical units during extended emergency incidents. These incidents include fire stand-bys, hazardous materials incidents, patient extrication from remote areas, and search and rescue operations. The team also supports non-emergency events such as parades, marathons, fireworks displays, street fairs, and cycling races. Team members undergo extensive training in Incident Command Systems, Weapons of Mass Destruction, Hazardous Materials Operations, and Public Safety Rehabilitation. Specialized equipment includes VHF, UHF, and low-band base radios, cellular telephones, cellular fax machines, cooling misters, chemical agent antidotes, portable stretchers, tents, bulk medical supplies, portable generators, portable lights, and oxygen administration equipment capable of serving up to 25 patients simultaneously. The team’s first deployment was during a hazardous materials incident at the Rockland County Health Complex in the fall of 2002, where they successfully triaged, evaluated, and treated over 100 patients alongside local EMS volunteers and other emergency management officials. RPS also manages Rockland Mobile Care/Regional EMS, which provides ambulance transportation and Advanced Life Support EMS for Orange and Rockland Counties in New York, as well as Pike County, Pennsylvania. In Pike County, Regional EMS operates as Medic 403, serving as the primary ALS provider for Westfall Township and Matamoras Borough, and as a secondary provider for Milford Township, Milford Borough, and Dingman Township upon request. Additionally, Regional EMS operates Hemlock Farms Advanced Life Support (Medic 403-H), a non-transporting fly-car contracted 24/7/365 to the Hemlock Farms Community Association, covering parts of Blooming Grove, Dingman, and Porter Townships.
